harmonicFunction: E (I) - Warm, open-string major tonic representing cherished memories in the verse
A / Aadd9 (IV) - Lush subdominant chord sharing the open B and high E strings with E major
C (bVI) - Borrowed flat-sixth chord that shatters the major-key warmth and ushers in the minor key
D (bVII) - Subtonic chord bridging the chorus and driving the outro loop
Em (i) - Parallel minor tonic where the song's heartbreak finally settles

techniques.name: Open-String Drone Strumming & Parallel Major-to-Minor Shifts
techniques.description: Fluid 16th-note acoustic/clean-electric strumming at 77 BPM that keeps the top two strings open across E and A before shifting into heavy, wide-open minor chords

sequence: Strum open E to Asus2/Aadd9 in the verse with a gentle 16th-note wave, letting the open B and E strings chime
Slide up to the 5th/7th-fret E-to-Aadd9 voicing (0-7-6-4-0-0 to X-0-7-6-0-0) for Stone Gossard's authentic intro shimmer
Drop cleanly into C major and E minor when the pre-chorus arrives
Build dynamic intensity on the Em - D - C outro cycle as the band swells toward the climax
tips: Keep your index finger anchored or lightly sliding on the 3rd string when moving between E and A shapes
At 77 BPM, think in 16th notes (1-e-&-a) so your strumming hand maintains a smooth, continuous pendulum motion
During the outro, let every chord ring out as wide as possible without rushing the tempo

sections.name: Intro & Verse Oscillation
sections.description: Tender E major to Asus2/Aadd9 oscillation that sets the reflective canvas of the verse.
notes: Let the open 1st and 2nd strings ring continuously across both chords
Use a soft, expressive pick attack in the opening bars
Try sliding the fretted notes on strings 3 and 4 up to frets 6 and 7 for Stone Gossard's signature color

sections.name: Chorus & Iconic Outro ('I Know Someday...')
sections.description: The harmony pivots into E minor for the emotional Em - D - C coda.
notes: Give D and C two beats each before holding Em for a full bar
Notice the emotional shock of hearing E minor after two minutes of E major
Gradually increase your strumming force as the outro builds

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.technique: Mike McCready Style E Minor Lead
sections.description: Soulful E minor pentatonic lead line in 12th position inspired by Mike McCready's outro solo.
notes: Play in the 12th-fret E minor pentatonic box with Hendrix/Gilmour-inspired passion
Hold long notes over the C major chord to let the harmonic tension bloom
Finish with wide, vocal-style vibrato on the root E (4th string 14th fret or 1st string 12th fret)

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul Standard (Stone Gossard) & Fender Stratocaster (Mike McCready) + Acoustic Guitar
guitar.pickup: Stratocaster neck single-coil for lead solo; warm humbucker or acoustic for rhythm

amp.recommended: Fender Bassman / Twin Reverb (clean rhythm) & Marshall JCM800 (lead)

settings.gain: 4 for rhythm (edge of breakup), 7 for McCready lead

effects.distortion: Ibanez Tube Screamer (TS9) into tube amp for the outro solo
effects.delay: Warm analog delay (340ms) on lead guitar
effects.reverb: Lush hall reverb (reflective of Ten's arena-sized mix)
effects.other: Dunlop Cry Baby Wah for expressive outro solo swells

beginner.title: Open-Chord Verse & Outro
steps: Master the two-chord verse loop: open E major to Asus2 (X-0-2-2-0-0)
Learn the C - Em pre-chorus shift and the D - C - Em outro loop
Play through the full arrangement from start to finish

intermediate.title: High-Neck Drone Voicings & Dynamic Swells
steps: Incorporate Stone Gossard's 4th-to-7th fret sliding E and Aadd9 shapes in the verse
Add expressive sus4 and bass-walk embellishments during the D - C - Em outro
Begin learning the opening phrases of Mike McCready's E minor pentatonic solo

advanced.title: Complete McCready Solo & Dual-Guitar Texture
steps: Perform Mike McCready's soaring outro solo with expressive full-step bends and wah inflections
Loop the D - C - Em rhythm progression and improvise dynamic E Aeolian/pentatonic solos
Capture every dynamic nuance from whisper-quiet intro to stadium-shaking finale

commonMistakes: Playing E minor in the verse by mistake—the verse is strictly in bright E major!
Rushing the slow 77 BPM tempo when the emotional outro kicks in
Muting the open B and high E strings during the verse E-to-Aadd9 changes
practiceRoutine: 3 minutes: E major to Asus2/Aadd9 open-string drone transition warmup
4 minutes: Pre-chorus and chorus C → D → Em transition practice
4 minutes: 16th-note strumming endurance and dynamic crescendo drill at 77 BPM
4 minutes: E minor pentatonic soloing over the D - C - Em outro loop
focusAreas: Emotional contrast between E major (verse) and E minor (chorus/outro)
Fluid 16th-note strumming at a slow ballad tempo (77 BPM)
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 77 BPM and subdivide into 16th notes so you don't rush the empty space
Practice the transition from the quiet verse into the heavy C - Em pre-chorus without speeding up
Record yourself playing the outro rhythm and solo over it in time
